    1. Matrix Data¶

    pyCirclize can plot a Chord Diagram(wiki) from matrix data like circlize or Circos Table Viewer.

    1-1. Example1 (3 x 6)¶

    This example uses the same matrix data as documented in circlize

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    import pandas as pd

from pycirclizely import Circos

# Create matrix dataframe (3 x 6)
row_names = ["S1", "S2", "S3"]
col_names = ["E1", "E2", "E3", "E4", "E5", "E6"]
matrix_data = [
    [4, 14, 13, 17, 5, 2],
    [7, 1, 6, 8, 12, 15],
    [9, 10, 3, 16, 11, 18],
]
matrix_df = pd.DataFrame(matrix_data, index=row_names, columns=col_names)

# Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot
circos = Circos.chord_diagram(
    matrix_df,
    start=-265,
    end=95,
    space=5,
    r_lim=(93, 100),
    cmap="T10",
    label_kws=dict(r=96, font=dict(size=12, color="white")),
    link_kws=dict(line=dict(color="black", width=0.5)),
)

print(matrix_df)
fig = circos.plotfig()
HTML(pio.to_html(fig, include_plotlyjs="cdn"))
    import pandas as pd from pycirclizely import Circos # Create matrix dataframe (3 x 6) row_names = ["S1", "S2", "S3"] col_names = ["E1", "E2", "E3", "E4", "E5", "E6"] matrix_data = [ [4, 14, 13, 17, 5, 2], [7, 1, 6, 8, 12, 15], [9, 10, 3, 16, 11, 18], ] matrix_df = pd.DataFrame(matrix_data, index=row_names, columns=col_names) # Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot circos = Circos.chord_diagram( matrix_df, start=-265, end=95, space=5, r_lim=(93, 100), cmap="T10", label_kws=dict(r=96, font=dict(size=12, color="white")), link_kws=dict(line=dict(color="black", width=0.5)), ) print(matrix_df) fig = circos.plotfig() HTML(pio.to_html(fig, include_plotlyjs="cdn"))

S1   4  14  13  17   5   2

from pycirclizely import Circos

# Create matrix data (10 x 10)
row_names = list("ABCDEFGHIJ")
col_names = row_names
matrix_data = [
    [51, 115, 60, 17, 120, 126, 115, 179, 127, 114],
    [108, 138, 165, 170, 85, 221, 75, 107, 203, 79],
    [108, 54, 72, 123, 84, 117, 106, 114, 50, 27],
    [62, 134, 28, 185, 199, 179, 74, 94, 116, 108],
    [211, 114, 49, 55, 202, 97, 10, 52, 99, 111],
    [87, 6, 101, 117, 124, 171, 110, 14, 175, 164],
    [167, 99, 109, 143, 98, 42, 95, 163, 134, 78],
    [88, 83, 136, 71, 122, 20, 38, 264, 225, 115],
    [145, 82, 87, 123, 121, 55, 80, 32, 50, 12],
    [122, 109, 84, 94, 133, 75, 71, 115, 60, 210],
]
matrix_df = pd.DataFrame(matrix_data, index=row_names, columns=col_names)

# Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot

    1-3. Example3 (10 x 2)¶

    This example uses the 10 x 2 matrix data randomly generated by Circos Table Viewer

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    import pandas as pd

from pycirclizely import Circos

# Create matrix data (10 x 2)
row_names = list("ABCDEFGHIJ")
col_names = list("KL")
matrix_data = [
    [83, 79],
    [90, 118],
    [165, 81],
    [121, 77],
    [187, 197],
    [177, 8],
    [141, 127],
    [29, 27],
    [95, 82],
    [107, 39],
]
matrix_df = pd.DataFrame(matrix_data, index=row_names, columns=col_names)


# Define link_kws handler function to customize each link property
def link_kws_handler(from_label: str, to_label: str):
    """Customize link properties based on the label."""
    if from_label in ("C", "G"):
        # Set opacity, layer orders higher than other links for highlighting
        return dict(opacity=0.5, layer="above")
    else:
        return dict(opacity=0.1, layer="below")


# Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot
circos = Circos.chord_diagram(
    matrix_df,
    space=2,
    cmap="Set3",
    label_kws=dict(font=dict(size=14)),
    link_kws=dict(direction=1, line=dict(color="black", width=0.5)),
    link_kws_handler=link_kws_handler,
)

print(matrix_df)
fig = circos.plotfig()
HTML(pio.to_html(fig, include_plotlyjs="cdn"))

    2. From-To Table Data¶

    pyCirclize can plot a Chord Diagram from from-to table data.

    2-1. Example 1¶

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    import pandas as pd

from pycirclizely import Circos
from pycirclizely.parser import Matrix

# Create from-to table dataframe & convert to matrix
fromto_table_df = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ["A", "B", 10],
        ["A", "C", 5],
        ["A", "D", 15],
        ["B", "D", 8],
        ["C", "D", 6],
    ],
    columns=["from", "to", "value"],  # Column name is optional
)
matrix = Matrix.parse_fromto_table(fromto_table_df)

# Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot
circos = Circos.chord_diagram(
    matrix,
    space=3,
    cmap=dict(A="royalblue", B="orange", C="green", D="red"),
    label_kws=dict(font=dict(size=14)),
)

print(fromto_table_df.to_string(index=False))
fig = circos.plotfig()
HTML(pio.to_html(fig, include_plotlyjs="cdn"))
    import pandas as pd from pycirclizely import Circos from pycirclizely.parser import Matrix # Create from-to table dataframe & convert to matrix fromto_table_df = pd.DataFrame( [ ["A", "B", 10], ["A", "C", 5], ["A", "D", 15], ["B", "D", 8], ["C", "D", 6], ], columns=["from", "to", "value"], # Column name is optional ) matrix = Matrix.parse_fromto_table(fromto_table_df) # Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot circos = Circos.chord_diagram( matrix, space=3, cmap=dict(A="royalblue", B="orange", C="green", D="red"), label_kws=dict(font=dict(size=14)), ) print(fromto_table_df.to_string(index=False)) fig = circos.plotfig() HTML(pio.to_html(fig, include_plotlyjs="cdn"))
    from to  value
   A  B     10
   A  C      5
   A  D     15
   B  D      8
   C  D      6
    Out[5]:

    2-2. Example 2¶

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    import pandas as pd

from pycirclizely import Circos
from pycirclizely.parser import Matrix

# Create from-to table dataframe & convert to matrix
fromto_table_df = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ["A", "B", 10],
        ["A", "C", 5],
        ["A", "D", 15],
        ["A", "E", 20],
        ["A", "F", 3],
        ["B", "A", 3],
        ["B", "G", 15],
        ["F", "D", 13],
        ["F", "E", 2],
        ["E", "A", 20],
        ["E", "D", 6],
    ],
    columns=["from", "to", "value"],  # Column name is optional
)
matrix = Matrix.parse_fromto_table(fromto_table_df)

# Initialize Circos instance for chord diagram plot
circos = Circos.chord_diagram(
    matrix,
    space=3,
    cmap="Viridis",
    ticks_interval=5,
    label_kws=dict(font=dict(size=14), r=110),
    link_kws=dict(direction=1, line=dict(color="black", width=0.5)),
)

print(fromto_table_df.to_string(index=False))
fig = circos.plotfig()
HTML(pio.to_html(fig, include_plotlyjs="cdn"))
